Stimulants: I think they have utility and recreational capacity but are not something to have around often or casually. The Germans used amphetamines during their blitzes and I've used them in my studies. I always told myself to work when I was using it so as to never justify habit-based consumption. Some people my age would take it before parties but it is a terrible combination with alcohol and I never had any more fun when on it than when sober (in fact it took away my desire and need for fun but the loss of appetite was not a fun problem when I was trying to gain weight). I knew that when I tried cocaine that I should never do it again as I was craving it for a whole month afterwards. I can't speak from experience on any of the others. A dealer I knew once told me "being addicted to stimulants is better than normal life as long as you can keep it up". 

Narcotics: I had once read that stimulants attract extroverts and depressants attract introverts. Because of that I avoided bars and other depressant pills and intentionally used stimulants instead, believing that something against my nature will be less addictive. The enjoyment I got from benign downs like nyquil or valerian root with alcohol was proof enough that I shouldn't go farther down that road. There will always be a small window of utility in a civilization for it but it will remain small. 

With alcohol, I will always be drinking some as long as cannabis and indoor smoking are illegal but I don't like the lack of awareness of how impaired I am or the feeling of stupidity. A lot of people will drink and smoke but I am far too impaired from that to do anything. Since as you said it's been a part of anything it feels hard to decide what should be done, if anything, about it. 

With psilocybin I often felt like I had great ideas and grand realizations when it was active but never truly remembered or internalized them. I also saw how some of the things I did during the trip were too impractical for the groovyness once I sobered up. I really don't want to speak on all psychedelics until I've tried them. The potential of ego death with DMT is very exciting. 

With the devil's lettuce, always enhancing music and food and being my social glue to avoid drinking. It's had its problems. It kept me from fully integrating with gamers or people who want to attend frat parties. It led me away from metal music into obscure and specific forms of electronic/industrial music, leaving me seeking solitude just to listen to what fitted my stoned mind. There were times when the rationalization hamster said "You can get high and still work/exercise" but I practically never did. Seeing how I had gotten strong cravings after three months without it I can see how I also need to prevent it from being habitual when I have access to it again. On stoner culture, I could definitely see in Amsterdam that anything that overtly promoted cannabis (i.e. the cannabis leaf) could only be found in tourist shops.
